mentions.sentence: Black-box testing and fuzzing have been used to identify various types of bugs in File systems and DBMSs, including crash inconsistency bugs [ 21,25], logic 203 PANGOLIN: a Comprehensive Testing Framework for Configuration-Rich Key-Value Stores SYSTOR ’25, September 8–9, 2025, Virtual, Israel bugs [ 31], and correctness bugs [ 3].
mentions.context_before: ack-box testing is a software testing method in which the functionalities of software applications are tested without having knowledge of internal code structure, implementation details, and internal code paths. Differed from black-box testing, modern fuzzing tools, such as AFL [ 8,39] and Nautilus [ 1], also employ light-weight instrumentation of the target program to collect some feedback about the generated inputs, which is used to guide the test case mutation process. More recently, leveraging grammar-based input generation greatly improved the performance of feedbackoriented fuzzers [ 1].
mentions.context_after: Compared with handwritten tests, these bug-finding tools have the capability to generate interesting test cases, including corner cases that are difficult for humans to contemplate, under acceptable overhead and little human effort involved. In principle, black-box testing and fuzzing can be routinely applied for systematically testing configuration-rich key-value stores. Unfortunately, our study of historical bugs in five widely used key-value stores reveals that generalpurpose testing tools can only identify a few bugs. analysis.summary: Pangolin tests configuration-rich key-value stores. The authors first study historical bugs in five mature stores over eight years and find that most could be caught by systematically testing a small sequence of operations and configurations. Pangolin turns that into a bounded testing strategy across black-box and fuzzing procedures, finding 20 bugs and reproducing 443 historical ones in RocksDB, LevelDB, HyperlevelDB, BadgerDB and Redis.
